messages:
sam: FYI did a perf run on the new kv-cache eviction path, and we're seeing a massive HBM bandwidth spike for very long seq requests (seq_len=32768). attached nsys.
anya: ugh, that sounds like cache thrash. did you capture the kernel timeline?
mike: which workload? streaming or full-generate?
sam: full-generate (non-streaming), batch=1, model=redwood-7b-qlora, reproducer: `./serve_bench --seq 32768 --batch 1 --kv-mode=on`. nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/trace_seq32k --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=cpu ./serve_bench --seq 32768 --batch 1
```
trace-bot: trace uploaded: https://perfetto.local/trace/abcd1234 (internal) :mag:
elena: I skimmed the trace: there's a repeating pattern where KV writebacks happen every 4k tokens and you get back-to-back large memcpy and memcpyAsync events. looks like we overflowed the per-shard cache window.
anya: can you paste the hot kernels section? even a short snippet helps.
sam: pasted excerpt from nsys report: 
```
Kernel                                             Calls  Total Time (ms)  Avg (ms)  GPU %  HBM BW (GB/s)
sm_gemm_128x128x8                                 4320   420.3             0.097     62.1   110.2
kv_writeback_chunk                                 512    120.4            0.235     18.7   680.7
cudaMemcpyAsync (HBM->HBM?)                        512    98.6             0.192     15.3   720.1
```
(we have a custom `kv_writeback_chunk` kernel)
mike: 700+ GB/s on the memcpy lines — that's basically saturating the card's HBM bursts and coincides with the GEMM stalls. looks like eviction plus refill thrash.
elena: especially bad because for long seq we append prefixes that force re-reads of the entire KV arrays per request. we should avoid doing a full refill for every request.
anya: is the KV cache pinned in GPU memory or doing CPU<->GPU bounce? the memcpy name is weird (HBM->HBM?), maybe we're moving between different GPU allocations or peer copies.
sam: allocations are on different CUDA contexts per worker thread right now (we have a per-request context create/destroy thing). that could be it. repro shows high device->device copies.
mike: quick mitigation: 1) reuse CUDA contexts per worker, 2) change eviction to LRU window that doesn't evict older layers for long seq, 3) cap batch size when seq_len > 8k. any objections?
anya: +1 on cap batch size. We should also consider switching to async prefetch and overlapping compute so refill doesn't block SMs. but if the bandwidth is saturated you'll still starve.
elena: I ran a microbenchmark: single worker, keep-alive context + pinned KV buffers cut the memcpy rate by ~6x for seq=32768.
sam: nice — can you drop the commands?
elena: sure:
```
# old: per-request allocs
for req in requests:
  ctx = create_context()
  alloc_kv(ctx, size)
  run_inference(ctx)
  destroy_context(ctx)

# new: keep-alive
ctx = create_context()
alloc_kv(ctx, max_size, pinned=True)
for req in requests:
  reuse_kv(ctx)
  run_inference(ctx)
```
mike: also spotted in nsys timeline: repeated `cudaMemsetAsync` on the KV buffers between batches — that's a red flag. zeroing whole buffer for each request is O(n) work; we can switch to token-range clears.
anya: agree. small fix: only clear the new segments written in this request and track tail pointer per-shard. that should reduce write traffic by ~4x for these cases.
sam: leaving this here as action items: 1) elena to prototype keep-alive contexts + pinned KV buffers (PR), 2) mike to guard `cudaMemset` calls with token-range checks, 3) anya to add a runtime cap to batching when seq_len>8192, 4) sam to run full nsys sweep after changes and post traces.
elena: starting a branch now, will post microbench numbers in this thread when ready.
trace-bot: perf comparison baseline vs PR_123: baseline HBM peak 720 GB/s, PR_123 peak 210 GB/s, mean latency down 3.4x :rocket:
anya: beautiful. once patches land, let's add a test in our perf CI: synthetic long-seq ray task that asserts HBM peak < 400 GB/s and latency < X.
mike: note for rollout: Dedicated customers hitting seq>16k should get auto-cap notification, maybe return 413 or suggest stream mode instead of failing silently.
sam: agreed. thanks folks — keeping the trace links in case we need to dig deeper: https://perfetto.local/trace/abcd1234 and https://nsys-reports/internal/1767004321-report.html
anya: :thumbsup:
